question: Should OpenClaw accept Android device-control, ADB-style access, or dynamic code execution from connected Android nodes, and should those be Android-specific commands or part of a generic node-advertised tool contract?
rationale: The remaining work changes phone authority, private-data access, and model-visible execution boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and security model.

options.title: Split and gate Android authority
options.body: Implement only narrow Android device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

options.title: Route through node-hosted tools
options.body: Use the generic node-hosted tool contract path before exposing Android ADB or dynamic execution as model-visible tools.

options.title: Keep high-power execution out of core
options.body: Reject ADB and dynamic Android code execution in OpenClaw core for now and require external plugins, ClawHub packages, or app-specific forks for that authority.

recommendation.title: Split and gate Android authority
recommendation.body: Implement only narrow Android device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.
